note: C, the six 3x3 buildings (art plan batch C), 2026-10-30. The planned route, create_map_object in style-matching mode inside a mock scene with a 48x48 inpainting mask, was tried three times (3 generations) and never drew a building: it continued the scene instead (see _map_object_tests). So the batch used the plan's fallback, one create_1_direction_object job at size 48 (10 generations, 16 candidates, palette = the 46 Apollo hexes, palette_name Apollo, view top-down, no style images: anchors are 32 px and would have shrunk the output), PixelLab review object f60b823f-f493-4fa0-80f8-fb8fc618f24e. All 16 frames are kept untouched in art/raw/c/candidates/frame_<i>.png (slot map in _slots); every frame came back 100% Apollo with no partial alpha. The 6 picks were promoted with select_object_frames (tag c_buildings) and saved as art/raw/c/<name>.png, byte-identical to their frames (_object = the promoted object). Anchor fields (art plan issue 11; not read by art:build): every rect is [x, y, w, h] in final 48 x 48 sprite pixels, after trim and bottom-centre placement. _light = the light-source spots. _pit = the elevator's dark shaft opening for the code-drawn cab. _chute = the body's outermost opaque pixel on each side at the tile centres x or y = 8, 24, 40 (N and S give y at x = 8/24/40, E and W give x at y = 8/24/40): a chute on that side and tile attaches there (the bodies are 35-42 px wide, so a chute placed on the 48 px footprint edge would float 3-5 px off the north, east and west faces).

_map_object_tests.note: create_map_object, style matching, custom inpainting mask, view high top-down, selective outline, medium shading, medium detail, 1 generation each. Backgrounds and masks: art/ref/c_scenes/ (c_hq*, made with scripts/art/mock.ts --b64). Raw results: art/raw/c/map_object_tests/. Review: node scripts/art/mapobj.ts <png> --rect <mask> --scene <scene> --out <prefix>.
_map_object_tests.1 e77177f3-26c0-4b67-a043-f8db120bd139: 144x144 L0 scene (c_hq.png), 48x48 mask at 48,48, two belts ending at the mask: returned the mask square 100% opaque as ground with the two belts joined by a corner piece. No building.
_map_object_tests.2 9a44b4cc-28d9-4f31-af5d-28cba56e8254: 112x112 'machine yard' (c_hq_t2.png: eight approved sprites around an empty 48x48 slot, no belts), mask at 32,32: returned 95% of the square as plain ground, every pixel identical to the background. No building.
_map_object_tests.3 d2ffe0c9-eec1-4377-a9ff-6e5210c8099b: the same yard with the code-drawn b_hq under the mask as a composition hint (c_hq_t3.png): returned ground again; the placeholder was painted out. No building.
_map_object_tests.verdict: In this mode the tool continues the background and ignores the description, whatever the context and whatever is under the mask; PixelLab's help desk says background_image is style context, not an inpainting canvas, and recommends a style-referenced object instead. So D and H skipped map_object too and went straight to their STYLE.md fallback.
